READ THIS FIRST
  Enabling a preset does not make a cluster compliant with HIPAA, SOC 2, PCI
  DSS or anything else.

  The mapping from these controls to any regulation has not been reviewed by
  anyone qualified.

  ControlsMet being True means one thing: every check this operator performs
  passed the last time it ran. It does not mean your cluster is compliant,
  secure, or audit-ready. Do not present it to an auditor as proof of
  compliance.

  pgaudit does not record an escalated session's reads and writes. Read the
  emergency access section before anyone uses it.

NOT CHECKED BY THE OPERATOR
  This list is not exhaustive. Anything that is not in the table above is not
  checked.
  - Everything about people and process.
  - Whether the audit is enough.
  - That the audit log cannot be altered.
  - Retention is not enforced.
  - Encryption at rest.
  - Certificates.
  - The network beyond the database pods.
  - Who can do what inside the database.
  - Emergency access, if you allow it.
  - The cluster around it.
  - Changes between checks, and checks that stop.
  The full lists are in docs/compliance.md and docs/emergency-access.md in the
  operator's repository.

EMERGENCY ACCESS
  WARNING: while you are escalated, your statements and their values are
  logged in clear text

  pgaudit does not record an escalated session's reads and writes.

  While escalated, the server writes every statement you run to its log, and
  it writes the values you bind to a statement's parameters there too, in
  clear text.

  This happens whatever the cluster's audit settings say: logParameters: false
  does not stop it.

  If you are using emergency access as part of an audit, your auditors will be
  able to read every value you used.

  These are the requests that exist now. A request that was deleted leaves
  nothing here. The server log, and the Kubernetes API server's audit log if
  you keep one, hold the rest of the record.

  No requests exist.
